title: The 'Buy Now Pay Later' Trap Is Getting Worse
summary: Finance YouTuber explains BNPL's mechanics and psychology, concluding the market itself is too small to cause a crisis but still harms individual borrowers.

assertions.quote: Psychologically, you now think you are saving $75, so it becomes a no-brainer to buy it today
41% of buy now pay later loans had a missing or late payment
57% of Americans using buy now pay later are doing so because they're trying to buy something they can't afford

verdicts.note: Multiple surveys report roughly 40-58% of users across different years citing affordability, not convenience, as their reason for using it.

Fed SHED: 29% of BNPL users cite 'only way I could afford it' as their main reason overall, rising to 40% for incomes under $25,000 versus 15% for incomes of $100,000+; it is the second most common main reason after spreading out payments (31%).
FEDS Notes: across the 2022-2023 SHED, 57% of BNPL users cited any necessity reason and 55% cited 'only way I could afford it' as one of their reasons for using BNPL.

assertions.quote: Klarna loses 24% of each purchase because of the origination fee
this whole tower is less than one block on this side

verdicts.note: Federal Reserve and Richmond Fed estimates put outstanding pay-in-four balances at roughly $3 billion against $1.2+ trillion in credit card debt.
KC Fed cites Worldpay data that BNPL was 4% of e-commerce and 1% of in-person purchase value in North America in 2021, projected to reach 9% and 2% by 2025 -- a small share of overall payment volume.

assertions.quote: if you rely on buy now pay later loans and constantly close out those accounts, your length of credit will never grow

verdicts.note: Length of credit history is a real scoring factor and short-lived accounts don't extend it the way an open revolving account does.

assertions.quote: Klarna now gives you the ability to pay over time for a fee ranging anywhere from zero to 36.99%

verdicts.note: Affirm and Klarna both disclose APRs that can reach into the 30% range on their longer financing products.
KC Fed endnote: longer-term BNPL loans (three months or more) may charge interest ranging from zero to nearly 30% APR, comparable to or higher than typical credit card rates.
